paper.title: Equal Opportunity in Online Classification with Partial Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online classification with partial (apple-tasting) feedback under gamma-EFP(delta) fairness at every round
unmapped: Apple tasting: true label observed only when the positive label is predicted; 0-1 loss

Fairness constraint (equalized false positive rates across two groups, w.r.t. the true distribution) must hold at every round with probability 1-delta; regret measured against the best gamma-EFP mixture of classifiers in a finite class H (|H| = N_exp) while the learner may be (gamma+beta)-fair
Oracle access to a cost-sensitive classification oracle for H
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t\in [T]$, our learner selects hypotheses from a hypothesis class $\H$ ... Environment draws $(x_t,y_t) \sim \mathcal{D}$ independently; learner observes $x_t$. Learner labels the point $\hat{y}_t = h_t(x_t)$ ... IF $\hat{y}_t = +1$ Learner observes $y_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online classification with partial feedback under fairness constraint (lower bound)
unmapped: Apple tasting: label observed only on positive prediction; 0-1 loss
Learner must satisfy T^{-alpha}-EFP(delta) at every round; regret against best 0-EFP mixture of classifiers
settings.definition_quote: any algorithm satisfying a $T^{-\alpha}$-EFP($\delta$) fairness constraint has expected regret with respect to the set of 0-EFP fair policies

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit over a (fair, support-2) policy class with approximate CSC oracle
unmapped: Policy class Pi consists of support-2 mixtures over finite H (|H| = N_exp); only an approximate CSC oracle over Pi is available
settings.definition_quote: The bandit algorithm, given access to an approximate-CSC oracle, runs in time polynomial in $T$ ...

algorithms.name: Explore (+1) then fair ILOVETOCONBANDITS with FairCSC oracle
Modified ILOVETOCONBANDITS with approximate CSC oracle (coordinate descent feasibility program)

symbols.gamma_fair: fairness level of the comparator class (gamma-EFP)
symbols.beta_fair: fairness slack: algorithm is (gamma+beta)-EFP(delta), beta = O(sqrt(ln(|H|/delta))/T^{1/4})

source.label: upper
source.quote: For any $\H$ and data distribution satisfying the two mild assumptions above, there exists an oracle-efficient algorithm that takes parameters $\delta \in [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}]$ and $\gamma \geq 0$ as input and satisfies $(\gamma + \beta)$-EFP($\delta$) fairness and has an expected regret at most $\tilde O(\sqrt{T} \ln(|\H|/\delta) )$ with respect to the class of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies, where $\beta = O(\sqrt{\ln(|\H|/\delta)}/T^{1/4})$.

results.notes: Regret defined through expectations over D (pseudo-regret). Comparator: best gamma-EFP mixture. Oracle-efficient (polynomial given CSC oracle).

symbols.beta_fair: any fairness slack beta > 0; algorithm is (gamma+beta)-EFP(delta)

conditions: Pr[a=j,y=-1] in Omega(1) for both groups
tuning: exploration length chosen as a function of beta

source.quote: More generally, we can extend Theorem~\ref{upper} to give an algorithm that satisfies $(\gamma + \beta)$-EFP($\delta$) for any $\beta > 0$, and achieves an expected regret at most $\tilde O\left(\frac{\ln(\frac{|\H|}{\delta})}{\beta^2} + \sqrt{T} \ln(|\H|/\delta) \right)$ with respect to the class of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies.

results.notes: Stated in a remark without proof.

symbols.alpha_tr: tradeoff exponent; fairness slack gamma'-gamma = O(T^{-alpha_tr})

conditions: the two mild assumptions of Section 3
tuning: exploration length modified according to alpha_tr

source.quote: it is straightforward, by modifying the length of the exploration round, to obtain a more general tradeoff---a regret bound of $O(T^{2\alpha})$ with respect to the set of $\gamma$-EFP fair policies, while satisfying $(\gamma + O(T^{-\alpha}))$-EFP($\delta$) fairness, for any $\alpha \in [1/4,1/2]$.

results.notes: Remark; log factors suppressed in the paper's statement.

conditions: comparator is the best policy in Pi (support-2 mixtures over H)

source.label: thm:bandit-regret
source.quote: The bandit algorithm, given access to an approximate-CSC oracle, runs in time polynomial in $T$ and achieves expected regret at most $O\left(\ln(|\H|T/\delta) ~ \sqrt{T}\right)$.

results.notes: Intermediate theorem for the contextual-bandit subroutine (after apple-tasting reduction).

symbols.alpha_tr: exponent: algorithm is T^{-alpha_tr}-EFP(delta) and competes with 0-EFP policies

source.label: thm:main-negative1
source.quote: Fix any $\alpha \in (0,0.5)$ and let $T \geq \sqrt[\alpha]{16}$. Fix any $\delta \leq 0.24$. There exists a hypothesis class $\H$ containing $\{\pm \mathbf{1}\}$ such that any algorithm satisfying a $T^{-\alpha}$-EFP($\delta$) fairness constraint has expected regret with respect to the set of 0-EFP fair policies of $\Omega\left(T^{2\alpha}\right)$.

results.notes: Algorithm class: all algorithms satisfying T^{-alpha}-EFP(delta). Lower bound construction uses two distributions with KL O(gamma^2).
